newsitem.title: USA: NEC, Bull launch smart card.
newsitem.headline: NEC, Bull launch smart card.

text.p: France's Cie des Machines Bull and NEC Corp of Japan said Tuesday they had launched the first in a series of smart cards that they planned to market throughout North America.

The companies said their divisions -- Bull Personal Transaction Systems and NEC Semiconductor Group -- had come out with Memphis, the first of a generation of cards designed for service and retail, among others sectors.

A smart card resembles a credit card, but also incorporates a microprocessor. It can store information like credits for members of a frequent flyer program, for example. It has more memory and security than a memory card, which can serve as a pre-paid calling card.
As part of their partnership, NEC will make the cards and Bull will market them, according to a Bull spokesman.
"NEC wants to become one the world's largest producers of these cards," he said, adding that the company planned to make about 100 million of them by 2000.
The spokesman said it was the first time that NEC was entering the smart card market.
He could not provide any of the partnership's financial terms and other officials were not immediately available for comment.
NEC Corp makes semiconductors, among other things, while Bull makes computer products like software and servers.
